source: USDA AMS Livestock, Poultry and Grain Market News, state hay reports
note: Confirmed trades as AMS reports them, $ per ton, by grade and bale type. Each report has its own date. Not blended with the NASS monthly prices in hay-prices.json.

reports.title: South Dakota Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Good to very good demand for all classes of hay. Best demand is coming from western South Dakota where the drought has been severe and little hay was made this year. Grass hay supplies are limited as the weather wasn't conducive to growing grass as it was dry during April and May.

reports.title: Alabama Direct Report (Bi-Weekly)
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Hay prices steady. Trade moderate, with good supply and moderate demand.

reports.title: Nebraska Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/23/2026
reports.comment: Compared to last report, trade activity was Light due to farmers harvesting corn and soybeans. Demand Good on all forages. Alfalfa ground and delivered prices unchanged. Dehydrated and sun-cured pellets of alfalfa prices remained unchanged. There were no comparable trades on all types of hay this period.

reports.title: Kansas Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/9/2026
reports.comment: Hay movement slowed this past week as much of the state received heavy rainfall. Demand remained high. Recent rainfall and warm temperatures have many producers anticipating another cutting of alfalfa.

reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Compared to the last report, Demand for hay remains high. We continue to see all types of hay being moved in preparation for fall and winter. Hay movement has slowed down due to the rain.

reports.title: Colorado Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/23/2026
reports.comment: Compared to last report: Trade activity Moderate. Demand Good to Very Good all markets of new crop hay. Premium small squares of alfalfa, alfalfa/grass mix, mixed grass, and prairie/meadow grass sold 25-50 cents/bale higher. Premium alfalfa 3x3's sold 20 $/bale higher this period. With corn silage harvest wrapping up, farmers have moved on to forage sorghum for silage and bales.

reports.title: Wyoming Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Compared to the last report all forages sold steady. Demand was moderate to good. Some previously spoken loads of hay have been turned back by out of state buyers due to the increase of diesel fuel and freight charges they can not afford to ship the hay halfway across the USA anymore.

reports.title: Idaho Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Demand for all types of hay in Idaho is moderate. Demand for straw is picking up but there aren't a lot of trades yet with buyers shopping around. Movement has been slower this week in Idaho with mostly small loads being bought. prices for alfalfa are steady.

reports.title: Oregon Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/23/2026
reports.comment: Compared to the last report, Movement has decreased throughout the whole state for all qualities of hay except small bales going to stables, they have a strong demand, decreased movement is expected to be due to the prices of fuel and people seem to be stocked up on their hay needs for thew time being. reports.title: Washington-Oregon (Columbia Basin) Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/16/2026
reports.comment: Compared to the last report, all grades of hay firm. Exporters especially China re-entering the market and domestic buyers with orders from Florida are active. Trade remains moderate to active with good demand.

reports.title: California Direct Hay Report
reports.heading: Direct Hay Weighted Average Report for week ending 10/23/2026
reports.comment: Compared to last report: Trade activity and demand were good on retail and dairy hay. In the North San Juaquin Valley and southeast regions, Retail alfalfa 3-tie bales sold $25/ton higher than two weeks ago. Dry cow and stock hay traded $5/ton higher. The next available hay report will be Friday, November 06, 2026.
